Avodah Zarah 70b:1.english: The Gemara relates: There was an incident involving a certain gentile girl who was found among wine barrels and she was holding wine foam in her hand. Rava said: The wine is permitted, as it is reasonable to say that she took it from the outside of the barrel and not from inside the barrel. And even if there is no more of the foam on the outside of the barrel, it is reasonable to say that she happened upon the foam while it was still there, even though it is no longer there.

Avodah Zarah 70b:10.english: The Gemara answers that Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: It is different there, as the *am ha'aretz* has a way to excuse his behavior if he were to be discovered reaching up to the upper roof, by saying: I merely stretched myself; I was not intending to tamper with anything.

Avodah Zarah 70b:11.english: Come and hear what is taught in that same *baraita*: If the roof of a ḥaver is beside the roof of an am ha’aretz, that ḥaver may lay out produce there and place vessels there, even if the hand of the am ha’aretz can reach the haver's roof. This poses a difficulty to Rav's statement. The Gemara answers that Rav could say to you: Isn’t there the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel, which aligns with my opinion with regard to roofs that are next to one another? What I say is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel's opinion.

Avodah Zarah 70b:12.hebrew: מתני׳ בולשת שנכנסה לעיר בשעת שלום חביות פתוחות אסורות סתומות מותרות בשעת מלחמה אלו ואלו מותרות לפי שאין פנאי לנסך.
Avodah Zarah 70b:12.english: MISHNA: In the case of a military unit [boleshet] that entered a city to stay there or collect taxes, if it entered during peacetime, then after the soldiers leave the open barrels of wine are forbidden, but the sealed barrels are permitted. If the unit entered in wartime, both these barrels and those barrels, even the open ones, are permitted, because in wartime there is no time for the soldiers to pour wine for idolatrous offerings, and one can be certain that the soldiers did not do so.

Avodah Zarah 70b:4.english: The Gemara relates: There was an incident involving a certain tavern keeper who transferred the key [iklida] to the door of her wine shop to a gentile woman. Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Elazar said: There was a similar incident that was brought before the Sages in the study hall, and they said: She transferred to her the responsibility for safeguarding the key alone but did not authorize her to enter the tavern, so there is no concern that she entered there.

Avodah Zarah 70b:6.english: The Gemara asks with regard to Abaye’s reasoning: Is this to say that the halakhot of pure items are more stringent than those concerning libation wine? The Gemara answers: Indeed, that is so. As it was stated that there was a dispute with regard to a courtyard whose owners divided it among themselves with a low partition (meseifas). Rav says: If one’s neighbor on the other side of the partition is an am ha’aretz, his pure items that he leaves in the courtyard are rendered impure, but in the case of a gentile neighbor, Rav says this does not render the Jew's wine an idolatrous libation. And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The pure items remain pure as well. Evidently, Rav considers the halakhot of purity more stringent than those of libation wine.

Avodah Zarah 70b:7.english: The Gemara raises an objection to Rav's opinion from a *baraita*: If the inner courtyard belongs to a ḥaver, i.e., one devoted to the meticulous observance of *mitzvot*, especially the *halakhot* of purity, *terumah*, and tithes, and the outer courtyard to an am ha’aretz, that ḥaver may lay out his produce there, in the inner courtyard, and place his vessels there, without concern that the *am ha'aretz* will touch the produce and vessels and render them impure. And this applies even if the hand of the am ha’aretz can reach there. This poses a difficulty to Rav's opinion, who holds that even in a situation with a partition, there is concern about contact with an *am ha'aretz*.

Avodah Zarah 70b:8.english: The Gemara answers that Rav could say to you: It is different there, as the *am ha'aretz* would be caught and accused as a thief if he were to tamper with the produce, as the *am ha'aretz* has no business being in the inner courtyard. Therefore, there is no concern that the *am ha'aretz* will tamper with the produce.

Avodah Zarah 70b:9.english: The Gemara suggests: Come and hear support for Rav’s opinion from a *baraita* (Tosefta, *Teharot* 9:11): Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: If the roof of a ḥaver is above the roof of his neighbor who is an am ha’aretz, that ḥaver may lay out produce there and place vessels there, provided that the hand of the am ha’aretz cannot reach the haver's roof; but if it is within the *am ha'aretz*'s reach, the *haver*'s pure items are rendered impure. This poses a difficulty to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who deems pure items permitted in a courtyard divided by a low partition.

Otzar Laazei Rashi, Talmud, Avodah Zarah.english:
1910 / (Avodah Zarah 70b) / *Imtzurei ka mimtzara*
Estendeillier: to stretch, to extend / [estendeillier] estendeilier
The foreign word appears after "Another interpretation: I am stretching myself," and refers to the movements of a person lying lazily and stretching their limbs for pleasure. The manuscript reads "mitmoded," which can also be interpreted as "stretching oneself," meaning to extend the limbs to their full length. Additionally, Rashi brings another version "imtzudi ka mimtzadna," apparently "I am turning on my side," and this also indicates an unintentional movement of the limbs.
✭ to stretch

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:11:1.hebrew: ספק ביאה – דלא ידעינן עובד כוכבים אי על, אי לא על, טהור. ומשום הכי שרי, דשני לן ספק ביאה מביאה ודאי וספק מגע.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:11:1.english: Uncertainty of entry - for we do not know if the gentile entered or did not enter, it is pure. And for this reason, it is permitted, because we differentiate between uncertainty of entry and certainty of entry, and uncertainty of contact.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:1.hebrew: בקעה – שדות הרבה זו אצל זו, בימות הגשמים שזרועה היא, ואין רבים דורסין אותה, והוי רשות היחיד לטומאה, וספיקא שאירעה בה הוי ספיקא טמא.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:1.english: Valley - many fields next to each other, in the rainy season when it is sown and many people do not tread upon it, and it is considered a private domain for impurity, and an uncertainty that occurred there is an uncertainty of impurity.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:2.hebrew: וטומאה בשדה פלונית – באחת מן השדות, ואין אנו יודעין איזו היא.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:2.english: And ritual impurity in such and such a field - in one of the fields, and we do not know which one it is.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:3.english: I walked to that place - in this valley.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:4.hebrew: ספק מגע טמא – דאמר: נכנסתי לשדה שהטומאה בה, ואיני יודע אם נגעתי בטומאה אם לאו.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:12:4.english: Uncertainty of contact, he is ritually impure - for he said: 'I entered the field where the impurity is, and I do not know if I touched the impurity or not.'

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:13:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא דפתחי חביות לשום ממונא – וכיון דחזו דחמרא הוא, פרשי, דבגניבותייהו טרידי ולא מנסכי.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:13:1.english: Since there are those who open barrels for the sake of money - and since they saw that it was wine, they refrained, for they are preoccupied with their thievery and do not pour libations.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:13:2.hebrew: הוי ספק ספיקא – ספק ישראל, ספק עובד כוכבים. ואת"ל עובד כוכבים, ספק נגע, ספק לא נגע. ובהא אפילו רבנן מודו. וכי פליגי רבנן עליה דר"א, היכי דמליא שדה טומאה, דאי על לה, לא אפשר דלא האהיל, דליכא אלא חד ספק.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:13:2.english: It is a compound uncertainty - it is uncertain whether they were Jews or gentiles. And even if you say they were gentiles, it is uncertain whether they touched it or did not touch it. And in this, even the Rabbis agree. And when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer, it is in a case where the field is full of impurity, for if he entered it, it is impossible that he did not overshadow it, as there is only one uncertainty.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:2:1.hebrew: דלהדי ביזעא שרי – אף בשתיה, דמירתת ולא נגע.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:2:1.english: Opposite the crack, it is permitted - even for drinking, as he would be afraid and would not touch it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:2:2.hebrew: דהאי גיסא והאי גיסא אסור – אף בהנאה. וכשאין נתפס על כניסתו כגנב, עסקינן שהיה לו חלק ביין, דאי נתפס עליו כגנב, כוליה שרי. ואית דגרסי: הוו ביזייני בדשא – חורין, וסדקין, ובקיעין. ובקעהו תרגומו: ובזעהו.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:2:2.english: On this side and that side, it is forbidden - even for benefit. We are dealing with a case where he is not caught as a thief upon his entry, as he had a share in the wine. For if he were caught as a thief, all of it would be permitted. And some versions read: 'There were *bizaynei* in the door' - holes, cracks, and fissures. And 'he split it' (בקעהו) its Aramaic translation is 'ובזעהו'.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:3:1.hebrew: ישראל בעליונה ועובד כוכבים בתחתונה – ויין בתחתונה, וישראל רואהו מלמעלה.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:3:1.english: A Jew in the upper story and a gentile in the lower story - and the wine is in the lower story, and the Jew sees it from above.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:3:2.hebrew: שרי – כל שרי דהכא, שרי אף בשתיה, דהא לא נגע קאמרינן. וכל אסיר דהכא, אף בהנאה. ובכולהו, הלכתא כרבא.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:3:2.english: Permitted - every 'permitted' here means permitted even for drinking, as we say he did not touch it. And every 'forbidden' here means forbidden even for benefit. And in all of these cases, the *halakha* is in accordance with Rava.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:1.hebrew: אי אית ליה לאישתמוטי – ולומר: לכך נכנסתי, סמכא דעתיה ולא מירתת. דכי על להך ביתא מעיקרא, אדעתא דלנסוכי על, וסבר: אי משכחו לי, אשתמיטנא. ואע"ג דבמגע היין לית ליה לאשתמוטי, אסור. דאי לאו לנסוכי על, למה ליה דעייל? ולא דמי למניח עובד כוכבים בחנותו, דהתם, דכיון דברשות עייל, וידעינן למאי עייל, כל זמן שלא הודיעו שמפליג, מותר, דסבר: אי נגענא, השתא אתי וחזי לי.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:1.english: If he has a way to excuse himself - and to say: 'I entered for this reason,' his mind is at ease and he is not afraid. For when he entered this house initially, he entered with the intention to pour a libation, and he thought: 'If they find me, I will excuse myself.' And even though he has no excuse for touching the wine, it is forbidden. For if he did not enter to pour a libation, why did he enter? And it is not similar to leaving a gentile in his store, for there, since he entered with permission and we know why he entered, as long as he did not inform him that he was leaving for a long time, it is permitted, for he thinks: 'If I touch it, he will come now and see me.'

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:2.hebrew: ואי לית ליה לאישתמוטי – שרי, וכיון דבהול הוא על כניסתו, מירתת ולא נגע.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:2.english: And if he does not have a way to excuse himself - it is permitted. And since he is anxious about his entry, he is afraid and does not touch it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:3.hebrew: ננעל הפונדק – ונתייחד עובד כוכבים עם היין, או שאמר ישראל לעובד כוכבים: שמור, עמוד מבחוץ ושמור.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:3.english: The inn was locked - and the gentile was secluded with the wine, or the Jew said to the gentile: 'Guard it, stand outside and guard it.'

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:4.hebrew: אסור – דחיישינן דלמא על, כיון דאמר לו: שמור, סמכא דעתיה דמפליג מיניה.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:5:4.english: Forbidden - for we are concerned that perhaps he entered, since he said to him: 'Guard it,' his mind was at ease that the Jew was leaving him.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:6:1.hebrew: שמע ישראל קל צלויי – ודוקא היין שעל הדולבקי שרי, כדתנן במתני'. ורבא קא משמע לן דקל צלויי כלא הודיעו שמפליג דמי. אי נמי, שאפילו על השולחן מותר, ובדלא אמר לו: הוי מזוג ושותה.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:6:1.english: The Jew heard the sound of praying - And specifically the wine on the *dolveki* (side table) is permitted, as we learned in the Mishna. And Rava teaches us that the sound of praying is considered as if he did not inform him that he was leaving for a long time. Alternatively, even the wine on the table is permitted, provided he did not say to him: 'Mix and drink.'

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:7:1.hebrew: שיפורא דבי שימשי – של ערב שבת, שהיו תוקעין להבדיל בין קדש לחול.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:7:1.english: Shofar of twilight - of Erev Shabbat, which they would blow to distinguish between the holy and the mundane.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:8:1.hebrew: ואי משום שבתא – ואם תאמר דסמכא דעתיה דעובד כוכבים משום דלא אתי ישראל בשבתא, האמר לי איסור גיורא כו'.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:8:1.english: And if because of Shabbat - And if you say that the gentile's mind is at ease because the Jew will not come on Shabbat, didn't Issur the Convert tell me etc.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:8:2.hebrew: פחות פחות מד' אמות – ועומד לפוש, וליכא עקירה מתחילת ד' לסוף ארבע.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70a:8:2.english: Less than four cubits at a time - and he stops to rest, and there is no continuous carrying from the beginning of four cubits to the end of four cubits.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:10:1.hebrew: אמצרי – דגג קמצרנא, אני מכוון למדת בניין שאני רוצה למדוד, לכך הושטתי את ידי. לשון אחר מתשובת הגאונים: מתמוגג אני, אשטנדלינ"ר בלע"ז, וגרסינן: אימצודי קא ממצדנא.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:11:1.hebrew: בצד גגו – שאינו גבוה ממנו, וליכא למימר: מתמוגג אני כשמושיט ידו שם.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:11:2.hebrew: אנא דאמרי כרשב"ג – דאמר לעיל: ובלבד שלא תהא ידו של עם הארץ מגעת שם. ולרב לא שני ליה בין שגג חבר למעלה בין שהוא שווה לו.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:12:1.hebrew: בולשת - חיל. על שם שמחפשין וחותרין, קרי להו בולשת, כדמתרגמינן: ויחפש ובלש.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:12:1.english: Boleshet - An army. They are called `boleshet` because they search and dig, as we translate [in Genesis 44:12]: 'and he searched and investigated'.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:1:3.hebrew: אימר מגבה דחביתא שקלתה – ודוקא רביתא, דאינה יודעת בטיב ניסוך ולא מסרה נפשה למינגע. אבל גדולה, מכי חזינן דנקיטא אופיא, לא תלינן לקולא.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:1:3.english: Say she took it from the outside of the barrel - And specifically a young girl, who does not know the nature of libations and would not risk touching it. But for an adult woman, since we see her holding foam, we do not attribute it leniently.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:1:4.hebrew: אע"ג דליכא תו – שאין שם אופיא עוד, ואיכא למימר: הא ודאי בגו חביתא שקלתה.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:1:4.english: Even if there is no more - that there is no more foam there, and one might say: 'She certainly took it from inside the barrel.'

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:1:5.hebrew: אימר איתרמי – דהך אופיא הוא דהואי התם.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:1:5.english: Say it happened to be there - that this foam was there.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:2:1.english: Pulmusa - the head of the troops, an army commander.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:2:2.hebrew: ולא ידענא אי – שרא משום ספק עובד כוכבים ספק ישראל, וכר"א דאמר: ספק ביאה טהור. ולקמיה פריך: הא לאו ספק ביאה הוא, דודאי עובדי כוכבים היו.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:2:2.english: And I do not know whether - he permitted it due to uncertainty whether they were gentiles or Jews, and in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer who says: 'Uncertainty of entry, it is pure.' And later it is asked: 'But this is not uncertainty of entry, for they were certainly gentiles.'

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:2:3.hebrew: ישראל נינהו – ואזלינן בתר רובא, דליכא ספיקא.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:2:3.english: They are Jews - and we follow the majority, so there is no uncertainty.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:3:1.hebrew: כיון דמפתחי טובא – הרבה יותר מכדי צורך שתייתן, מוכחא מילתא דאדעתא דממונא פתחו, ובגנבותייהו טרידי ולא מנסכי. ודמי לבולשת שנכנסה לעיר בשעת מלחמה, דקתני מתניתין: אלו ואלו מותרות. הלכך, אע"ג דספק מגע הוא, כיון דמוכחא מילתא לקולא, כספק ביאה דמי.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:3:1.english: Since they opened many - much more than needed for their drinking, it is proven that they opened them with the intention of finding money, and they are preoccupied with their thievery and do not pour libations. And it is similar to a raiding party that entered a city during wartime, as the Mishna teaches: 'Both these and those are permitted.' Therefore, even though it is an uncertainty of contact, since the matter is proven leniently, it is considered like an uncertainty of entry.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:4:1.hebrew: מסוביתא – מוכרת יין בחנות, כמו "זולל וסובא" (דברים כא), "סבאך מהול במים" (ישעיה א).
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:4:1.english: Masuvita - a wine seller in a shop, like "glutton and drunkard" (Deuteronomy 21:20), "your wine is cut with water" (Isaiah 1:22).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:4:2.hebrew: אקלידא – מפתח, שמירת מפתחות, ולא סמכא דעתה ליכנס ונתפסה כגנב.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:4:2.english: Iklida - a key, for guarding keys, and her mind was not at ease to enter, and she would be caught as a thief.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:5:1.hebrew: יין נסך מיבעיא – בניחותא, ומסייע לרב דימי.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:5:1.english: Is wine for a libation necessary? - This is said with ease, and it supports Rav Dimi.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:6:1.hebrew: למימרא דטהרות אלימי מיין נסך – מדנקט לה בלשון קל וחומר.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:6:2.hebrew: שחלקה במסיפס – מחיצה נמוכה, עם הארץ מצד זה, וחבר שטהר טהרות מצד זה.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:6:3.hebrew: אינו עושה יין נסך – דנתפס עליו כגנב. אלמא, טהרות אלימי.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:7:1.hebrew: מיתיבי – שתי חצרות זו לפנים מזו, הפנימית של חבר.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:7:2.hebrew: וחיצונה – הפתוחה לרשות הרבים, של עם הארץ, דאין לו לעם הארץ דריסת הרגל על הפנימית.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:7:3.hebrew: שוטח שם – בפנימית. אבל אי הוי איפכא, דחיצונה של חבר, כיון דהוי לעם הארץ דריסת הרגל בחיצונה, אין חבר שוטח שם פירותיו. מכל מקום, קשיא לרב, דקתני: אף על פי שידו של עם הארץ מגעת לשם.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 70b:8:1.hebrew: התם משום דנתפס עליו כגנב – דמה לו בפנימית? אבל חלוקה, דכחצר אחד דמי, כי עייל ידיה לא מתפיס כגנב.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Avodah Zarah 70.english: If the roof of a *haver* is beside or lower than the roof of an *am ha'aretz*, any place where the *am ha'aretz* can reach out and touch is presumed to be impure, in accordance with the statement of the first *tanna* in the *Tosefta*. With regard to a gentile, the Rambam says that if there is a low partition between them, the Jew need not be concerned with regard to either libation wine or impurity (Rambam *Sefer Tahara*, *Hilkhot Metamei Mishkav UMoshav* 12:19 and *Kesef Mishne* there, and *Sefer Kedusha*, *Hilkhot Ma'akhalot Assurot* 13:7; *Shulchan Arukh*, *Yoreh De'a* 129:16).

A *meseifas* is a small partition that is not ten handbreadths high. It serves to define each person's part in the courtyard, but it is not considered a complete partition such that the neighbor would be accused of being a thief if he enters the other side of the partition (see *Bava Batra* 6b). Therefore, regarding libation wine, since even the gentile knows that this part of the courtyard belongs to his fellow, the gentile is ashamed to enter there. For this reason, if we did not see the gentile there, we do not suspect that he touched the wine. However, if it is known that he entered there, there is a concern, since he would not be accused of being a thief. This is not the case for pure items, which are impure in any case since he would not be accused of being a thief (Ra'avad).

If the roof of a *haver* is above the roof of an *am ha'aretz*, the *haver* may lay out his vessels and his pure produce there, and they retain their status even if the *am ha'aretz* can reach out his hand to touch them. This applies to a gentile as well, if the Jew's courtyard is above the gentile's, and he need not be concerned either with regard to impurity or with regard to libation wine. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel (Rambam *Sefer Tahara*, *Hilkhot Metamei Mishkav UMoshav* 12:19 and *Kesef Mishne* there).

Steinsaltz comment #2 on Avodah Zarah 70.english: The Ramban (and several other early authorities) summarize that there are four main different laws regarding this matter. The first case is when the gentile has no connection to the wine or to the house where the wine is located. In this case, even if the gentile is found standing next to the wine, there is no concern that he touched it. The second case is when the gentile has a connection to the wine but not to the house. If the gentile is found next to the wine, there is a concern that he touched it. The third case is when the gentile has a connection to the house (or has permission to be there) but not to the wine. There is a concern for the wine unless it was guarded, or the wine was locked or sealed. The fourth case is when the gentile has permission for both the wine and the house. In this situation, the wine is only permitted if there were Jews constantly watching the gentile and ensuring he did not touch it.

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Avodah Zarah 70.english: In a courtyard divided by a *meseifas* (a light fence), with a *haver* on one side and an *am ha'aretz* on the other side, the *haver*'s pure items are pure even if the *am ha'aretz*'s hand can reach there, because they are in the *haver*'s domain. If there was a gentile on one side and an Israelite on the other side, and there was a *meseifas* between them, even if the gentile's hand reaches the Israelite's portion, there is no concern for libation wine or for pure items. This is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan's words (Rambam *Sefer Tahara*, *Hilkhot Metamei Mishkav UMoshav* 12:21; *Sefer Kedusha*, *Hilkhot Ma'akhalot Assurot* 13:7; *Shulchan Arukh*, *Yoreh De'a* 129:16).

Steinsaltz comment #4 on Avodah Zarah 70.english: Early commentators offer several interpretations for this word, and there is no certainty regarding its origin, which is certainly from a foreign language. Some believe (R.B.) that its origin is in Greek *mesoporos*, meaning something hollow in its middle, which aligns with the Geonim's interpretation that a *meseifas* is a wall full of windows. Others say its origin is in Latin *sepes*, meaning a fence or partition, or in Greek *psephos*. However, it is likely related to the Greek root *mesos*, meaning middle, something that stands in between.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:10.english: They answer: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: It is different there, as the *am ha'aretz* has a way to excuse himself if he is found reaching his hand to the upper roof. He would say: I only want to stretch myself, and that is why I raised my hand, but I did not intend to do anything.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:11.english: They propose: Come and hear a proof from what we learned: If the roof of a *haver* is beside the roof of an *am ha'aretz*, that *haver* may lay out produce and place vessels there, even if the *am ha'aretz*'s hand can reach the *haver*'s roof. This is a difficulty for Rav! They answer: Rav could say to you: Is there not the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel which aligns with my view regarding adjacent roofs? What I say is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's opinion.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:12.english: MISHNA: A boleshet (military unit) that entered a city to stay there or collect taxes, if it was during peacetime, open wine barrels are forbidden; if they were sealed, they are permitted. If it was in wartime, both these and those are permitted, even the open ones, because the soldiers have no time to pour libations.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:6.english: They question the very assumption in Abaye's words: Is this to say that pure items are more stringent than libation wine? They answer: Indeed, as it was stated that they disagreed on this matter: A courtyard whose owners divided it with a *meseifas*, a thin, small barrier less than ten handbreadths high. Rav says: If there was an *am ha'aretz* on the other side, the *haver*'s pure items in the other part of the courtyard are impure. But if there was a gentile on the other side, the gentile does not render the wine a libation. And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The pure items remain pure as well. In any case, we see from here that according to Rav's view, they are more stringent regarding pure items than they are concerned about libation wine.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:7.english: Regarding Rav's view concerning pure items, they raise an objection from what we learned: There were two courtyards, one inside the other. The inner courtyard belonged to a *haver* who was meticulous in the laws of purity, and the outer courtyard belonged to an *am ha'aretz* who was not meticulous in them. That *haver* may lay out produce and place vessels there in the inner courtyard, even if the *am ha'aretz*'s hand can reach there. If so, this is a difficulty for Rav's opinion, for even in a place with a division and a partition, he is concerned about the *am ha'aretz*'s touch!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:8.english: They answer: Rav could say to you: It is different there, as the *am ha'aretz* would be caught as a thief. For in the inner courtyard, the *am ha'aretz* has no business at all, and if he enters there, he is considered a thief. Therefore, we do not suspect that he would do so.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 70b:9.english: They propose: Come and hear a proof for Rav's opinion from what we learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: If the roof of a *haver* is above the roof of an *am ha'aretz*, that *haver* may lay out produce and place vessels there, provided that the hand of the *am ha'aretz* cannot reach the *haver*'s roof. For if the *am ha'aretz*'s hand can reach, the *haver*'s pure items are impure. If so, this is a difficulty for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who permitted pure items in a courtyard divided by a *meseifas*!
